meta_description: Free Scratch programming course. 35 projects from the Raspberry Pi Foundation curriculum. Techbase, Ibadan, Nigeria.
eyebrow: Free Course · Beginner · Ages 8–16 · Ibadan, Nigeria
hero_sub_html: Block-based visual coding from MIT. Build games, animations, music, quizzes and interactive stories across 35 hands-on projects from the official Raspberry Pi Foundation Scratch curriculum.

about.label: About This Course
paras_html: Scratch is a visual programming language from MIT designed to make coding fun and accessible. Instead of typing, you drag and drop coloured blocks — making it perfect for beginners, especially young learners aged 8–16. No previous experience needed.

This course follows the official Raspberry Pi Foundation Scratch curriculum. Every project links to the official guide at projects.raspberrypi.org where you'll find starter files, worked examples and extension activities. Designed and compiled by Babatunde Awoyemi, Techbase Consultant Services, Ibadan.
bullets_html: Sprites, backdrops and navigating the Scratch editor
Motion, Looks, Sound and Events blocks
Pen extension for drawing and generative art
Cloning for creating many sprite instances
Building real games, stories and interactive tools
about.kit_note: All projects run entirely in the browser — no software to install. Each project page has an orange button that opens the official Raspberry Pi guide.

steps.p_html: Go to scratch.mit.edu in any browser. Create a free account — no download or install needed.
Click any card above to open the project page. Start at 01 or jump to any level — each is self-contained.
Click the orange 🍓 button to go to the official guide and starter project on projects.raspberrypi.org.
Follow the guide, remix the starter, and try the extension challenges. Share your finished project online.
